text:
Myth: Google is out to get small businesses with its new Business Profile rules.

Reality: Google has a spam problem.

Scammers put fake phone numbers on posts and photos so people ring the wrong business.

Honest businesses are just getting caught in the net.

9pm. Someone on the couch taps your Facebook ad and submits the form. Ten seconds of effort.

Next morning you call. No answer.
After lunch. Voicemail.

By Thursday they've booked with the clinic down the road that called first.

Stop typing your mobile number at the bottom of your Google Business Profile posts.

Your profile already has your verified number.

Use the "Call now" or "Book" button instead. That's what it's there for, and it won't get your post pulled.

Before you touch anything else in Google Ads, check your conversion tracking.

If Google can't see which clicks turned into calls or enquiries, it's guessing.

And a guessing machine with your credit card is not a great combination.

"Cheapest electrician in Perth, call now for 20% off"

vs

"Family-owned electrical business servicing Wanneroo, Joondalup and the northern suburbs since 2012"

Only one belongs in your Google Business Profile description.

https://gimsresults.com.au/post/google-business-profile-posts-rejected

Your Google Business Profile isn't only yours.

Customers can suggest changes. Competitors can. Someone who half remembers your hours can.

When did you last check the list of managers on your profile? Recognise everyone on it?
